content.text: Asset: Directory and core payment system accounts
Threat: A former employee or contractor signs in with a still-active account
Vulnerability: Offboarding is manual and not linked to the HR leaver event
6.5 Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
Treatment plan: Disable accounts automatically from the HR leaver event; weekly reconciliation report
R-002: No periodic user access review
Asset: Core payment system access rights
Threat: Access rights accumulate and are never challenged
Vulnerability: No scheduled recertification of who has which role
Treatment plan: Quarterly access recertification signed by each system owner
Asset: Server and database administrator accounts
Threat: Administrator actions cannot be attributed to a person
Vulnerability: Admin passwords are shared in a team spreadsheet
Treatment plan: Named admin accounts with a password vault and session logging
R-004: Excessive privileges in the core payment system
Threat: An operator misuses rights to release or alter payments
Vulnerability: Roles are broad; operators can both prepare and release payments
Treatment plan: Redesign roles around least privilege and remove unused rights

summary.after: [R-004] Excessive privileges in the core payment system

content.text: R-005: Phishing leads to credential theft
Asset: Staff mailboxes and SSO accounts
Threat: Phishing e-mail captures staff credentials
Vulnerability: MFA is not enforced everywhere and awareness training is annual only
6.3 Information security awareness, education and training
Treatment plan: Phishing-resistant MFA for all staff, quarterly training and simulations
Threat: Attacker exploits a known vulnerability in the VPN appliance
Vulnerability: Firmware is patched quarterly, with no emergency patch process
Treatment plan: Monthly patch window and a 72-hour emergency patch SLA for critical issues
Threat: Data cannot be recovered after a failure or corruption
Vulnerability: Restores have never been tested end to end
Treatment plan: Quarterly documented restore test against the payment database
R-008: Ransomware on file servers and endpoints
Asset: File servers and staff endpoints
Threat: Ransomware encrypts data and halts operations
Vulnerability: Flat network, uneven endpoint protection, backups reachable from the domain
Treatment plan: Network segmentation, EDR on all endpoints, offline backup copy

summary.after: [R-008] Ransomware on file servers and endpoints

content.text: Asset: Object storage holding settlement files
Threat: Settlement files are exposed publicly by a misconfigured bucket
Vulnerability: No configuration baseline or automated checks on storage settings
5.23 Information security for use of cloud services
Treatment plan: Policy-as-code checks that block public buckets; weekly drift scan
Threat: The processor is unavailable and payments cannot be authorised
Vulnerability: Single processor, no fallback route, weak contractual remedies
5.22 Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
Treatment plan: Transfer part of the loss through SLA credits and business interruption insurance; agree a fallback processor
R-011: Weak security terms in vendor contracts
Threat: A supplier incident affects Larkspur without contractual recourse
Vulnerability: Older contracts lack security, audit and incident notification clauses
5.20 Addressing information security within supplier agreements
5.22 Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
Treatment plan: Standard security addendum; renegotiate the ten most critical suppliers

summary.after: [R-011] Weak security terms in vendor contracts

content.text: Asset: Core payment system and network logs
Threat: Malicious activity goes unnoticed for weeks
Vulnerability: Logs stay on each host and nobody reviews them
Treatment plan: Onboard core systems to a central log platform with alerting and a review rota
R-013: Insecure code in the merchant portal
Threat: Injection or access control flaws expose merchant data
Vulnerability: No automated code scanning or security review before release
8.29 Security testing in development and acceptance
Treatment plan: Add SAST and dependency scanning to CI and a pre-release security test

summary.after: [R-013] Insecure code in the merchant portal

content.text: R-014: Test environments hold real card data
Threat: Real card numbers leak from weakly protected test systems
Vulnerability: Production data is copied to test for debugging
Treatment plan: Stop copying production data; use a synthetic data generator and masking

summary.after: [R-014] Test environments hold real card data

content.text: Threat: A laptop with company data is lost or stolen
Vulnerability: Disk encryption is not enforced on all laptops
Treatment plan: Enforce full-disk encryption and remote wipe through device management
R-016: Insider fraud through missing segregation of duties
Asset: Payment initiation and approval workflow
Threat: One person creates and approves a fraudulent payment
Vulnerability: Initiation and approval can be done by the same user
Treatment plan: Four-eyes approval for payments above a threshold, enforced in the system

summary.after: [R-016] Insider fraud through missing segregation of duties

content.text: Asset: Public payment API and website
Threat: A volumetric attack makes the payment API unavailable
Vulnerability: Capacity depends on the ISP; no dedicated scrubbing service
Treatment plan: Rely on ISP-level mitigation for now; revisit at the annual risk review
Asset: Encryption keys for card and customer data
Threat: Keys are exposed or lost, so data is exposed or unrecoverable
Vulnerability: Keys are stored beside the data they protect with no rotation
Treatment plan: Move keys to a managed KMS or HSM with rotation and access logging
R-019: Personal data kept longer than needed
Threat: Excess personal data is exposed in a breach or breaks data protection rules
Vulnerability: No retention schedule and no automated deletion
Treatment plan: Approve a retention schedule and automate deletion for the main stores

summary.after: [R-019] Personal data kept longer than needed

content.text: Threat: A security incident is handled late or badly
Vulnerability: No documented plan, roles or contact tree; no exercises
5.24 Information security incident management planning and preparation
5.25 Assessment and decision on information security events
Treatment plan: Write the incident response plan, assign roles and run a tabletop exercise
Threat: An unreviewed change breaks or compromises production
Vulnerability: Emergency changes can be deployed without approval or later review
Treatment plan: Require a ticket and a second reviewer for all production changes; review emergency changes weekly
R-022: Uncontrolled access to the server room
Threat: An unauthorised person gets physical access to servers
Vulnerability: A shared door code is used and entries are not logged
Treatment plan: Badge access with entry logs and a monthly log review

summary.after: [R-022] Uncontrolled access to the server room

content.text: R-023: Misuse of privileged utility programs
Threat: An administrator uses a utility to bypass application controls
Vulnerability: Utilities are available to all administrators
Treatment plan: Utilities limited to the admin group and logged; remaining risk accepted
R-024: Clock drift breaks log correlation
Threat: Events cannot be correlated across systems during an investigation
Vulnerability: Not all devices synchronise to the same time source
Treatment plan: Remaining devices tolerated until the next refresh; remaining risk accepted
